canonical_topic: Where NGLs come from and LPG definition
definition: NGLs are commonly dissolved within crude oil or natural gas and are separated out at natural-gas-processing plants (from gas) or at refineries (from crude oil).
core_idea: Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) is a specific term for a mixture of the two heaviest common NGLs, propane and butane.
key_points: NGLs are abundant in shale deposits developed via fracking.
Separation occurs at gas-processing plants (from natural gas) or refineries (from crude oil).
LPG = a propane/butane mixture, a subset term within the broader NGL category.
relationships: LPG is a specific propane+butane blend within the broader NGL family
caveats: LPG is not synonymous with all NGLs — it specifically refers to the propane/butane mix.
